correctness.rationale: For all integers p>=2 and n>=6p-3, admissible orbit pairs are confined to explicit index blocks by cycle-distance inequalities. The blocks are cones with proven universal pole apices; a single bridge appears only for two vertex-axis fixed points. Counts of contractible components imply the traces by simplicial Lefschetz and equivariant Alexander duality. The rotation formula and degree concentration are already proved in the complete prior public cyclic result, not reasserted as independent discoveries. A new standalone verifier ran successfully on 126 parameter/axis cases, 6447 dual fixed faces and 21 independent direct ordinary-cut chain-character cases. The finite tests are not infinite proofs; the proof contains the quantifier/boundary arguments.

originality.rationale: The nearest complete public result proves exactly the cyclic rotation character but expressly excludes dihedral reflections; restricting a D_n character to C_n does not determine its reflection values or D_n-fixed dimension. The source paper supplies shellability and a Betti count. The reflection-fixed Alexander-dual geometry and axis-dependent formulas add genuinely missing information for all p>=2 and n>=6p-3. Existing unpowered-cycle dihedral results concern p=1, which does not imply the formula for powered cycles. Original publisher full text inaccessible; risk acknowledged.
residual_risks: Original full 2603.23155 and Bayer primary PDFs could not be exhaustively inspected; the Oxford institutional tool reported disconnected VPN.
An equivalent unpublished or unindexed computation might exist despite overlapping parameter/alias searches.

value.rationale: The geometric cone-and-bridge decomposition settles the fixed-space topology of the dual for every reflection in a two-parameter infinite family, and produces all missing D_n character values and invariant homology dimensions. Neither ordinary Betti counts nor the published cyclic representation determine these; two axis types at even n yield distinct traces. This is not a cosmetic restatement or single finite numeric increase.
